title: Async policy mismatch caused hidden canary shadowing and rollback failure
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a scheduled canary rollout for model v2025-02-b, an async promotion policy mismatch between the control plane and edge routing caused an invisible shadow canary to receive a subset of traffic while the primary canary was marked as failed. Attempts to rollback were blocked by a stale version-pin held by the shard coordinator, resulting in degraded responses and a 17-minute elevated error window for some customers. This ticket contains the incident timeline, root cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-12T09:07Z - Canary rollout for model v2025-02-b initiated (traffic ramp to 5%).
2025-02-12T09:10Z - Initial health checks reported increased latency (SLO breach alarm).
2025-02-12T09:11Z - Control plane flagged canary unhealthy and initiated rollback path; edge routing reported continued mixed-serve from a shadow variant (not the flagged canary).
2025-02-12T09:12Z - On-call routed; found routing table divergence: async-promotion policy enabled on control plane but not on several edge proxies due to a recent configmap partial rollout.
2025-02-12T09:14Z - Kubernetes configmap refresh completed on majority, but one shard coordinator still held an old version-pin preventing clean rollback (version pin persisted in shard metastore).
2025-02-12T09:20Z - Attempts to force-unpin via orchestration API failed with lease conflict; manual intervention required.
2025-02-12T09:25Z - Temporary traffic gate deployed to route affected customers to fallback model variant; error rate returned to baseline over next 10 minutes.
2025-02-12T09:37Z - Full rollback completed after manual unpin and orchestrator resync; canary marked failed and traffic normalized.
2025-02-12T10:00Z - Incident declared resolved; postmortem workstream opened.
2025-02-14 - Initial RCA draft reviewed by runtime and orchestration teams.
2025-02-18 - Design review of stronger rollout gating and config distribution strategy completed; engineering implementation in progress.
impact: Approximately 17 minutes of elevated 5xx and latency for 2% of production traffic (estimate based on request logs). Two enterprise customers reported degraded model responses impacting user-facing features. No data exfiltration or security breach observed.
root_cause: Three contributing issues: (1) a partial configmap rollout left an async-promotion flag out-of-sync between control plane and a subset of edge proxies; (2) shard coordinator metastore retained a stale version-pin after a prior failed promotion, blocking automated rollback; (3) orchestration API exposes a race when forcing unpin under concurrent lease renewal which caused manual intervention to be required.
mitigation: Short term: deployed a traffic gate to route affected customers to a stable fallback variant and performed a manual unpin/resync on the affected shard coordinator. Medium term: enforce atomic config rollout via config-version checks, add a fast-path 'emergency-unpin' with stronger fencing semantics, and improve canary health signals to prefer aggregated cross-shard quorum before automatic rollback.
action_items: ENG-314160: Implement config-version handshake for rollout (owner: Priya Menon, due: 2025-02-28)
ENG-314161: Add emergency-unpin API with strict lease fencing and audit log (owner: Tomás Alvarez, due: 2025-03-07)
ENG-314162: KV metastore compaction job to evict stale pins older than 48h (owner: Marco Li, due: 2025-03-05)
ENG-314163: Update canary health aggregator to require cross-shard quorum before auto-rollback (owner: Aisha Kapoor, due: 2025-03-03)
ENG-314164: Run tabletop drill for mixed-config rollouts and recovery runbook (owner: SRE Team, due: 2025-03-10)
ENG-314165: Instrument per-shard routing telemetry and alerting for early detection of shadow variants (owner: DataDog Integration, due: 2025-03-01)
DOC-314166: Write a short runbook section describing manual unpin procedure and RBAC constraints (owner: Technical Writing, due: 2025-02-25)
notes: Review discovered a small UX gap: operators cannot see per-shard config version from the Console; add a short term Console surface for config sync state.
We observed that the older shard coordinator was a transient node created after a rolling upgrade; add upgrade-time preflight to ensure metastore migrations cleared pins.
Consider adding automated chaos tests for partial configmap application to catch out-of-sync promotion flags during CI.
Security review not required for rollback changes, but emergency-unpin API will include additional audit logging as a precaution.
